title: Local magnitude history gave no clear added size estimate gain for shallow ComCat M5.5+ events in 2013-2025
abstract: We tested whether prior local mean magnitude improves the chance estimate that a shallow M5.5+ earthquake reaches M6.0. We used a fixed ComCat snapshot and ridge logistic fits. The baseline used location groups and the prior local event count. The added input was a mean magnitude with five prior pseudo-events. History covered lags greater than 1 day and up to 365 days within 500 km. Fits used 5,204 events in 2001-2012. Tests used 4,838 events in 2013-2025. Added magnitude history raised log loss by 0.0393%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for loss reduction was -0.0829% to +0.0120%. No planned check gave a clear positive gain. Some checks gave small losses. The test thus gives no clear added size estimate skill for this input and model. It does not establish magnitude independence or predict earthquake times. Revised records, coarse location controls, mixed magnitude types, one model and 13 test years limit inference. Code, aggregate scores, source hashes, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit are included. External event records and derived event tables remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Added magnitude history gave no clear positive gain in log loss. The bars show conditional 95% three-year block limits. Positive values mean lower error. The right panel shows each test year.
